value.behaviour: checkReactVersion warns once, linking to the React 18 migration guide, when the app's React major version is below 18.
rules: 1. Keep the function name, the try/catch with the /* ignored */ catch, the comment and the require.resolve('react/package.json', { paths: [targetPaths.rootDir] }) and require(reactPkgPath) lines exactly as they are, so line numbers before them do not move.
2. Compute const major = parseInt(reactPkg.version, 10); and warn only when major < 18 (a NaN major never warns).

3. The warning is one console.log(chalk.yellow(...)) of a template literal reading: You are using React ${reactPkg.version}, which is no longer supported by Backstage. Please upgrade your app to React 18 by following the migration guide: https://backstage.io/docs/tutorials/react18-migration/
4. No emoji box and no mention of React 16 or 17 remain; the call site checkReactVersion() in serveBundle is unchanged.

sites.rule: Rules 2 to 4: the major computation and the single warning, inside the existing try block.

The React 18 migration guide states that React 17 is no longer supported and React 18 is the minimum version.
rules: 1. The :::info admonition reads: Backstage packages require React 18. React 17 is no longer supported, and the Backstage CLI shows a warning when your app uses an older version of React.

2. The intro paragraph says Backstage core libraries and plugins declare ^18.0.0 as their peer range for react, react-dom and @types/react (code style), and that a project still on React 17 must follow this guide before it upgrades to a Backstage release that requires React 18.

3. In the plugin package.json examples, the highlight-add devDependencies lines are "@types/react": "^18.0.0", "react": "^18.0.2", "react-dom": "^18.0.2", and the highlight-add peerDependencies lines are "^18.0.0" for all three.
4. Remove the :::info admonition that suggests keeping React 17 devDependencies in individual plugins.
5. Follow docs/contribute/doc-style-guide.md: present tense, active voice, address the reader as you, no statements about the future.

sites.first_line: This guide has been updated to include steps for removing support for React 16, as it is now deprecated.

The Backstage core libraries and plugins are compatible with all versions of React from v17 to v18. This means that you can migrate projects at your own pace. We do however encourage you to do so sooner rather than later, both to keep up with the evolving ecosystem, but also because React 18 brings performance improvements, in particular in tests.
